report.summary: Chunk 9 of worktree.py: allocation path and resolved root checks, cleanup_worktree docstring and first lines.
risks: _refuse_if_repo_adjacent | medium | Called with worktree_path and resolved_root; if either implementation is wrong, containment could be violated. | Verify that _refuse_if_repo_adjacent raises for paths inside the repo checkout.
_lexical(root) | medium | Used multiple times; if _lexical does not normalize properly, path checks may be incorrect. | Confirm _lexical normalizes separators and resolves symlinks consistently.
Path(os.path.realpath(str(_lexical(root)))) | medium | realpath can fail or follow unexpected junctions; the exception handling may mask issues. | Test with junctions and symlinks in root path.
cleanup_worktree | medium | The chunk shows only the first lines; the rest of the method is missing, so partial removal and race handling cannot be verified. | Review entire cleanup_worktree method.
todos: Verify that _refuse_if_repo_adjacent is defined and correctly identifies repo adjacency.
Ensure that _lexical normalizes paths as expected (e.g., resolves '..', removes redundant separators).
Test allocation with junctions in DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT to confirm resolved_root check catches them.
Complete review of cleanup_worktree method for race condition handling.

handoff.purpose: Allocation path and resolved root containment checks; start of cleanup_worktree.

symbols.name: allocate_worktree
symbols.note: Creates worktree directory, runs git worktree add, records allocation.

symbols.name: cleanup_worktree
symbols.note: Removes allocated worktree directory and prunes git worktree; only first lines shown.

claims.text: An allocation that cannot be contained is refused before anything is created: `..` in a branch name would otherwise place a candidate worktree (and later, a recursive delete) outside the root.
claims.why: The code calls _refuse_if_repo_adjacent(worktree_path, ...) and checks escape with _is_within before creating anything.

claims.text: ORDER IS DELIBERATE, and it is what makes each of these testable on its own. "Is this inside the developer's checkout?" is the worst answer, so it is asked FIRST and named precisely; asking it after the escape check would make it unreachable, because a path that escapes the root INTO the checkout would already have been refused with the generic reason.
claims.why: The code calls _refuse_if_repo_adjacent(worktree_path, 'allocation path') before the escape check (_is_within).

claims.text: WHAT IS NOT HERE, and why. There used to be a second lexical call, `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent(_lexical(root), "worktree root")`. It is DOMINATED -- 0 counterexamples in 216,225 enumerated (root, repo, branch) shapes -- but NOT for the reason an earlier version of this comment gave. That version claimed the allocation-path check on the line below covers everything the root check did. It does not: with the RESOLVED-root check disabled, 955 of those shapes survive, every one of the form "the root is a strict ANCESTOR of the checkout and the allocation path is a sibling of it" (root C:/a, repo C:/a/a, branch tb). The allocation path in those is repo-adjacent to nothing, so the line below stays silent.
claims.why: The claim references a removed check and a resolved-root check that is not fully visible in this chunk. The resolved-root check appears later but its behavior depends on _refuse_if_repo_adjacent which is not defined here.

claims.text: What actually covers them is the RESOLVED-root check further down: on a genuine ancestor chain with no reparse points, realpath is the identity map, so the resolved root is still that strict ancestor and `_refuse_if_repo_adjacent` fires on it. The removed guard is dominated by the pair, not by the allocation path alone -- and its replacement is not dominated in return, because it also catches the case the whole lexical pair was blind to (a junction inside DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT).
claims.why: The claim depends on the behavior of _refuse_if_repo_adjacent and the resolved-root check; neither is fully defined in this chunk.

claims.text: `_worktree_root_for` is PURE TEXT -- it reads an env var and appends a digest -- so a single junction anywhere in DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT lands the entire worktree root inside the developer's checkout while every lexical check above passes. `cleanup_worktree` catches that case (step 4), but only when it is time to delete: by then the candidate has already been created inside the checkout and its files are in the developer's `git status`. Creation is where that has to be refused.
claims.why: The claim references _worktree_root_for and cleanup_worktree step 4, which are not in this chunk.

claims.text: The target must be PROVEN to be a worktree this manager allocated (see :meth:`_require_allocated_worktree`); anything else raises without removing a thing. The removal itself is done here rather than by ``git worktree remove --force``, which follows reparse points planted inside the tree; ``git worktree prune`` then deregisters it.
claims.why: The docstring describes behavior that depends on _require_allocated_worktree and git commands not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: The candidate BRANCH is deliberately left alone here -- see :meth:`reap_branches` for why deleting it in this call would be wrong.
claims.why: References reap_branches, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Raises: WorktreeContainmentError: If the target cannot be proven to be an allocated worktree, or if the primary checkout is no longer the directory this manager was created for. Nothing is removed in either case.
claims.why: The actual raising of WorktreeContainmentError is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Raises: WorktreeRemovalRace: If a reparse point appeared above the removal while it was underway. The tree is PARTIALLY removed and that is what the exception says; it is deliberately not repaired.
claims.why: The actual raising of WorktreeRemovalRace is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Raises: RuntimeError: If the worktree directory could not be removed. A failed removal is never swallowed silently.
claims.why: The actual raising of RuntimeError is not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Asked FIRST, before the target is even examined: if the primary checkout has moved, nothing this method could prove about the target is worth acting on. See the method for what this does and does not cover -- it is a mitigation for the move-in attack, not a closure.

observations.what: The chunk contains a large comment explaining the ordering of checks and historical removal of a guard. The resolved-root check is present, but the removed check's behavior is only described.
cleanup_worktree docstring claims that WorktreeRemovalRace can be raised if a reparse point appears above the removal while underway, but the actual implementation is not shown in this chunk.
The allocation path check uses _is_within(worktree_path, _lexical(root)); if _lexical does not resolve symlinks, a path with symlinks could bypass this check.
